- **Recommendations:**
  - Detector architecture for HTP v68. Use a conv-only, anchor-free, single-scale (stride 8) detector in the CenterNet/FCOS/YOLOX style; write your own or start from Apache-2.0 YOLOX, avoiding AGPL Ultralytics. Input is a static NCHW [B,1,H,W] dB spectrogram tile. Stem: space-to-depth 4x4 then Conv2d to >= 32 channels. All channel counts multiples of 32. ReLU or ReLU6 (HardSwish is acceptable) instead of SiLU. BatchNorm folded. No LSTM, GRU or attention in v1. If context is needed, add one depthwise/dilated conv block or a LayerNorm-free attention variant later, and only after profiling.
  - Output contract. Emit raw logits and regressions as SEPARATE output tensors: an objectness/heatmap tensor, a box tensor (dt_start, dt_stop, df_low, df_high), and class logits, each with its own quantization encoding. Do NOT put Sigmoid, Softmax, decode, TopK or NMS inside the HTP graph: the 2.42 runtime lacks the Softmax cDSP crash fix (2.47), and NMS needs all data in TCM/2. Run decode and NMS on the CPU (NumPy or C++, under 1 ms for a few hundred candidates).
  - Tile geometry from the VTCM rule at a 2 MB budget: A8 tiles up to 1024 frequency bins wide (512 if A16) by 256-512 time rows, with about 64 bins of frequency overlap and about 25% time overlap. Never feed a full 4096/8192-bin row as one tile. Normalise dB to a fixed range (for example a noise-floor-relative clamp of 0-80 dB mapped to 0-1) so one static input scale is valid across gains and SDRs.
  - Compile every graph with VTCM = 2 MB: ORT provider option vtcm_mb='2', qnn-context-binary-generator --vtcm_override 2, or backend-extension graphs.vtcm_mb=2. Set htp_arch=68. Test soc_model 35 vs 93. Set session.disable_cpu_ep_fallback=1 so partial offload fails loudly. Leave the default (4 MB) nowhere.
  - Pin two complete runtime sets and choose by golden test plus an 8 h soak. Set A, documented by Radxa: QAIRT 2.42.0.251225 (qcom-qnn-sdk-v68 0.1.0-2) + Radxa onnxruntime_qnn 1.23.2 cp312 + x86-64 Ubuntu 22.04 / Py3.10 host for qairt-converter/quantizer. Set B, community-proven: onnxruntime 1.27.0 + onnxruntime-qnn 2.3.0 (bundled QAIRT 2.47.0), which adds per-channel and W8A16 and makes the official ARM-Linux 2.47 host tools usable on the Q6A itself. Install each set in its own venv with its own ADSP_LIBRARY_PATH. Record SHA-256 of libQnnHtp, the V68 stub and skel, and every context binary, as PrismPhi does.
  - Primary training-to-deploy path (no x86 needed per new class): train or fine-tune in PyTorch (home-base GPU for full training; Q6A CPU for head fine-tuning). Export ONNX opset 17-21 with static shapes. Quantize to QDQ with onnxruntime.quantization get_qnn_qdq_config (QUInt8 activations, symmetric int8 weights; QUInt16 activation overrides only where needed), or AIMET-torch QAT with aimet_torch.onnx.export(prequantize_constants=True). Load with ORT QNN EP on the Q6A with ep.context_enable=1 to cache the compiled context. Evaluate, then promote. Secondary path for Set A: an x86 host with QAIRT 2.42 converter/quantizer produces a DLC, then the on-device qnn-context-binary-generator --dlc_path ... --vtcm_override 2 produces the context, run with qnn-net-run.
  - Quantisation policy: start with PTQ w8a8 on 500-1000 calibration tiles that span all SDRs, gains, RBWs, empty-band noise and every class. If per-class AP@0.5 on device falls more than 2-3 points below FP32, try A16W8 (on Set B, with tile width <= 512), then QAT. Always judge on HTP outputs, not CPU QDQ simulation: v68 shows device-specific output offsets. Keep a per-class confusion and IoU report for FP32-CPU, QDQ-CPU and HTP.
  - Use AI Hub only from the home base and only for runtime-neutral outputs: submit_quantize_job (AIMET, GPU) to get QDQ ONNX, compile to ONNX/TFLite, and profile on the RB3 Gen 2 Vision Kit as a reference latency. Do not use its qnn_dlc or context artifacts with Set A (no QAIRT 2.42 on AI Hub since about 22 Jun 2026; DLC and context are only forward-compatible). Upload only spectrogram tiles or synthetic data, never demodulated content.
  - NPU budget: plan on about 10 ms per 512-640 px YOLOv8n-size tile on the Q6A end to end (AI Hub NPU-only: 3.6-4.7 ms at 640). Size the detector to about a third or a half of YOLOv8n FLOPs for 56 Msps spans, which need about 40-85 tiles/s at 4096-8192 FFT with 8-16x averaging. Run the NPU at <= 50% duty and update overlay boxes at 2-10 Hz with tracking or interpolation on the 20-30 fps waterfall. RTL-SDR spans (2.4 Msps, 3 tiles across) need only about 9 tiles/s. Measure the real per-call overhead with qnn-net-run --profiling_level basic and qnn-throughput-net-run before fixing tile and batch sizes. Batch tiles (prepare batch 4-8, or variable batch once verified on the pinned runtime).
  - IQ second stage: keep the small Conv2d(1xK) classifier on the CPU (ORT CPU) by default. Move it to HTP only if batching 32-64 detected boxes per call, because a 2-channel IQ input is a low-depth activation and per-call FastRPC overhead dominates. If it goes to HTP, make the stem output >= 32 channels and keep fixed window lengths.
  - Recovery plan: (1) Run the NPU worker as a separate process that owns the FastRPC session. Tiles arrive over a shared-memory ring, results go back over a Unix socket, with a heartbeat per inference. (2) Watchdog: kill and restart the worker if one inference exceeds max(500 ms, 5x p99), or on any QNN_COMMON_ERR_SYSTEM_COMMUNICATION or crash. Allow >= 15 s after a CDSP crash (SSR wait is 5 s in <= 2.47 and 11 s in 2.48+; the kernel auto-recovers the cdsp remoteproc). (3) After 3 restarts in 60 s, restart the CDSP via /sys/class/remoteproc/*/state and cdsprpcd, then switch to the ORT-CPU copy of the same QDQ model at a reduced tile rate, and flag it in the UI. (4) At boot and after every recovery, run a golden tile and compare outputs against stored references within tolerance. (5) Never run two HTP contexts in parallel or multi-threaded on 2.42; recording never depends on the NPU process.
  - Versioned class growth: give each model release a manifest holding the class list, training-data SigMF annotation hashes, calibration-set hash, runtime-set id and hashes, and the context binary. To add a class, retrain (head-only fine-tune first, full retrain if recall on old classes drops), re-quantize with a calibration set that includes the new class, recompile, and gate promotion on the regression set for all old classes plus the golden test. Keep the previous model for one-tap rollback.
- **Numbers:**
  - Device QAIRT runtime: 2.42.0.251225 (libQnnHtpPrepare.so build string v2.42.0.251225135753_193295); qcom-qnn-sdk-v68 0.1.0-2 deb = 44,221,844 bytes, installed 168,655 KB; libQnnHtpPrepare.so = 87.3 MB (aarch64)
  - QAIRT release months: 2.42 Dec 2025, 2.45 Mar 2026, 2.47 May 2026 (ARM-Linux host: Ubuntu 24.04 + Python 3.12), 2.48 Jun 2026, 2.49 Jul 2026, 2.50 Aug 2026; onnxruntime-qnn 2.7.0 (13 Oct 2026) targets QAIRT 2.51
  - AI Hub QAIRT availability: 2.42 default+latest (26 Jan 2026); 2.42/2.43/2.45 (14 Apr 2026); 2.45/2.46/2.47 (22 Jun 2026); 2.50 added and 2.47 removed (14 Sep 2026); qnn_context_binary target removed 14 Sep 2026; QCS6490 (Proxy) removed 26 Jan 2026 in favour of the real RB3 Gen 2 Vision Kit
  - SoC ids (current QNN table): SM7325/778G = 35 (V68), QCM6490 = 93 (V68), SM8350 = 30 (V68)
  - VTCM: QNN default graph request 4 MB (0 = SoC max); Q6A rejects a 4,194,304-byte request (err 0x138d); about 2 MB usable per users; byte-granularity requests only on v81+, in multiples of 64 KB
  - TCM conv-fit (3x3, A8): W=512 D=32 needs 0.39 MB; W=1024 D=32 needs 0.77 MB; W=2048 D=32 needs 1.52 MB; W=4096 D=32 needs 3.04 MB; at A16 the needs double (W=1024 D=32 is 1.53 MB). Budget is TCM/2 = 1 MB at 2 MB VTCM
  - HTP layout granularity: channels rounded to 32, width to 8 (u8) or 4 (u16), height to 8; INT16 weights limited to 0x8000..0x7F7F (A16W16, v73+ only)
  - AI Hub QCS6490 latencies (QAIRT 2.50 assets): MobileNet-v2 224 w8a8 1.06-1.33 ms, w8a16 1.81 ms; ResNet18 w8a8 1.48-1.89 ms; YOLOv8n-size 640 w8a8 3.6-4.7 ms, w8a16 10.5-18.7 ms; YOLO-X 640 w8a8 7.1-12.2 ms; YOLOv7 640 w8a8 7.0-7.4 ms; ViT-224 w8a8 56 ms, w8a16 30 ms; MobileViT w8a16 9.7 ms; UNet 640x1280 w8a8 about 243 ms; FFNet-40S 2048x1024 w8a8 33-49 ms
  - Q6A community latencies: YOLOv8n INT8 about 10 ms (Frigate, QAIRT 2.46); official YOLOv8n context 10-12 ms vs about 20 ms self-built; Qwen3.5-0.8B decode about 7.4 tok/s (QNN EP 2.3 / QAIRT 2.47, vtcm_mb=2)
  - Spectrogram geometry at 56 Msps: NFFT 4096 gives 13.67 kHz bins and 73.1 us per frame (27,344 frames/s at 50% overlap); NFFT 8192 gives 6.84 kHz and 146 us. At 2.4 Msps, NFFT 1024 gives 2.34 kHz bins
  - Estimated tile load (512x512 tiles, 64-bin frequency overlap, 25% time overlap, 50% FFT overlap): 2.4 Msps/1024/avg4: about 9 tiles/s; 20 Msps/4096/avg8: about 29 tiles/s; 56 Msps/4096/avg16: about 40 tiles/s; 56 Msps/8192/avg8: about 85 tiles/s (my calculation)
  - QNN SSR recovery wait: 5 s up to 2.47, 11 s from 2.48
  - Calibration size: AI Hub recommends 500-1000 samples; the audit plan used 200-500 windows
  - Package versions (Oct 2026): aimet-torch 2.41.0 (py310-none-any, BSD-3); aimet-onnx 2.41.0 (x86_64 only); qai-hub 0.56.0; onnxruntime 1.31.0 (aarch64 wheels); onnxruntime-qnn aarch64 wheels since 2.1.0 (Apr 2026); torch 2.14.1 (aarch64 wheels); ai-edge-litert 2.3.0 (aarch64); TorchSig 2.2.0 (MIT); sigmf 1.13.0 (LGPL-3.0)
- **Rejected:**
  1.
    - **Name:** AI Hub qnn_dlc / context-binary artifacts for the 2.42 runtime
    - **Why:** AI Hub has not offered QAIRT 2.42 since about 22 Jun 2026. As of 14 Sep 2026 the versions are about 2.48-2.50. DLC and context binaries only run on the same or a newer runtime, and Q6A users get 'Using newer context binary on old SDK' (0x1388).
  2.
    - **Name:** Running qairt-converter/qairt-quantizer 2.42 on the Q6A
    - **Why:** ARM-Linux host support was added only in QAIRT 2.47, and Radxa documents x86-64 Ubuntu 22.04 for 2.42. Using 2.47 host tools produces artifacts the 2.42 runtime cannot load.
  3.
    - **Name:** FP16 / FP32 graphs on the HTP
    - **Why:** The QCS6490 v68 firmware rejects them ('SocModel doesn't support FP16'). FP16 on v68 is an automotive SA8295P feature.
  4.
    - **Name:** A16W16 quantisation
    - **Why:** 16-bit activations with 16-bit weights require minimum arch V73.
  5.
    - **Name:** Default 4 MB VTCM compilation
    - **Why:** Rejected on the Q6A ('vtcm size 4194304 unsupported'). Only about 2 MB is usable.
  6.
    - **Name:** Full-span tiles (4096-8192 bins wide) in one inference
    - **Why:** The TCM conv-fit rule exceeds the 2 MB VTCM budget (3.0 MB or more at A8 for a 32-channel stem).
  7.
    - **Name:** GRU/LSTM-based detectors or classifiers on 2.42
    - **Why:** Forward-only and rank-3 limits; converter quantization bugs fixed only in 2.46; unrolling passes only from 2.45; not in ORT QNN EP's documented op list.
  8.
    - **Name:** Transformer/DETR-style or full-resolution UNet detectors
    - **Why:** ViT-224 costs 56 ms (w8a8) and UNet 640x1280 costs about 243 ms on QCS6490. A dynamic uint16 MatMul mis-lowering was seen on v68. MaskedSoftmax and KV features are unsupported on v68.
  9.
    - **Name:** Softmax, Sigmoid decode, TopK or NMS inside the HTP graph
    - **Why:** 2.42 lacks the Softmax cDSP crash fix (2.47). NMS needs all data in TCM/2. Separate quantized outputs are needed anyway to avoid the shared-scale collapse.
  10.
    - **Name:** Ultralytics YOLOv8/YOLOv11 as the shipped detector
    - **Why:** AGPL-3.0 licence, and its SiLU activations are not in the HTP fused-activation list. Use an Apache-2.0 YOLOX-style or self-written conv detector.
  11.
    - **Name:** onnxruntime-qnn 2.7.0 (QAIRT 2.51) or qai_appbuilder 2.48.40 as the default runtime
    - **Why:** Not tested on the Q6A. Reports conflict on 2.46+ with CDSP c4-00004. Only 2.3.0 (QAIRT 2.47) has a public Q6A success. Keep these as experiments behind the golden test.
  12.
    - **Name:** sigqnn (PyPI)
    - **Why:** A placeholder package, self-described as 'NOT FUNCTIONAL'.
  13.
    - **Name:** Concurrent multi-threaded or multi-context HTP inference on 2.42
    - **Why:** Hang and crash fixes for parallel DLC init (2.47) and heavy concurrent inference (2.48) are missing from 2.42.
- **Open questions:**
  - What is QCS6490's physical VTCM size, and why is only about 2 MB grantable on the Q6A (firmware partition, PD type, another client)? Query it with QnnDevice_getPlatformInfo (on-chip device info includes VTCM MB) or qnn-platform-validator.
  - Does the QAIRT 2.47 set (ORT 1.27.0 + onnxruntime-qnn 2.3.0) survive an 8 h soak on kernel 6.18.2-4 with the golden firmware? Do 2.48-2.51 load at all (needed to reuse AI Hub artifacts)? Reports conflict (Dual-O vs PrismPhi).
  - Do the official QAIRT 2.47+ ARM-Linux host tools (qairt-converter, quantizer, context generation) actually install and run on the Q6A under Ubuntu 24.04 / Py3.12, and how much RAM and time do they need for a 1-3 M-parameter detector?
  - Which soc_model value does each pinned runtime expect for QCS6490: 35 (SM7325) as used by the community, or 93 (QCM6490 in current docs)? Does a mismatch change performance or prepare behaviour?
  - Is the variable-batch feature (execute with n x prepared batch) present in 2.42, and what is the per-call FastRPC overhead for small graphs on the Q6A? This sets the tile batching strategy.
  - Does on-device online prepare by the ORT QNN EP 1.23.2 (libQnnHtpPrepare) compile a detector reliably, given the segfault reports (forum 31046) and context-generator crashes (31368)?
  - Does the ORT 1.23.2 QNN EP accept per-channel int8 weights and AIMET opset-21 QDQ exports? One user claims per-channel needs ORT 1.24+.
  - Do v68 channel-wise zero-input output offsets (seen in FC layers by PrismPhi) also affect conv detection heads, and what is the scale per class?
  - What causes the zeroed class channels after quantizing a multi-class YOLO head on the Q6A (forum 31368)? Calibration coverage, near-constant maps, or a converter bug?
  - Is A16W8 usable on the 2.42 runtime, or only on 2.47+? There is no public 2.42 test.
  - What does the Radxa ARM64 Docker image radxazifeng278/qairt-npu-v68:v1.2 contain (QAIRT version, converter tools)? Not inspected because of the Docker Hub rate limit.
- **Notes:** I used 6 WebSearch calls. Most evidence comes from primary pages I downloaded and parsed: Qualcomm QAIRT docs (published Sep 2026, so they describe 2.5x, not 2.42), the AI Hub docs and release notes, Radxa's docs, the Radxa qcom-qnn-sdk-v68 deb (I listed its contents and checked the binaries' architecture, version strings and CLI options), PyPI metadata, Hugging Face Qualcomm model cards, and Radxa forum JSON.
  
  The op-support tables do not carry per-arch columns, so v68 limits come from the 'minimum arch' notes in HtpOpDefSupplement.
  
  The most important new finding beyond the earlier audit is PrismPhi's Sep 2026 Q6A port. It ran the official onnxruntime-qnn 2.3.0 (QAIRT 2.47) on stock firmware with W8A16 and vtcm_mb=2. That contradicts the 'QAIRT 2.46+ fails' report. Combined with 2.47's official ARM-Linux host support, it suggests a fully on-device toolchain may be possible, but it is unverified beyond one user.
  
  The second key finding is that AI Hub can no longer target QAIRT 2.42, so its QNN outputs are unusable with the Radxa-pinned runtime.
  
  The tile and NPU-budget figures are my own calculations from Qualcomm's TCM rule and AI Hub latencies. They are estimates to validate with qnn-net-run profiling on the device.
  
  Files I downloaded for verification are under /tmp/claude-0/-home-user-lizbeth307/f89a86b4-fa51-5ce8-96da-e73d5f771cf3/scratchpad (dl_htp, dl_aihub, dl_radxa, dl_deb, dl_ort, dl_perf, dl_forum, dl_prism). The calculation scripts are /tmp/claude-0/-home-user-lizbeth307/f89a86b4-fa51-5ce8-96da-e73d5f771cf3/scratchpad/scripts/budget.py and /tmp/claude-0/-home-user-lizbeth307/f89a86b4-fa51-5ce8-96da-e73d5f771cf3/scratchpad/scripts/ops.py.

## npu:data_labelling (run `wf_62c18130-b0d`)

- **Area:** On-device collection and labelling of spectrogram (waterfall) training data: SigMF box annotations, auto-labelling from known context, a touch labelling UI, dataset versioning, balancing and splits, augmentation, storage budget, privacy and licences
- **Findings:**
  1.
    - **Name:** SigMF v1.2.6 annotations as the canonical box format
    - **Role:** Single source of truth for every labelled signal box (time x frequency) on the waterfall
    - **Details:** Verified on sigmf.org: the spec is v1.2.6. Each annotation segment has sample_start (required) and sample_count, which give time. freq_lower_edge and freq_upper_edge are in Hz and are RF values when the frequency is known; they must be given together or not at all. The segment also has label, comment, generator and uuid. The spec RECOMMENDS keeping label to 20 characters or fewer. Annotations MUST be sorted by sample_start. Global fields include sha512 (hash of the dataset file), recorder and geolocation, a GeoJSON point; the captures-scope geolocation is preferred. Datatypes cover the native SDR formats: cu8 for the RTL-SDR, and ci16_le or ci8 for the LimeSDR in CS16 or CS8. Extensions go in a namespace that has a version and is declared in core:extensions as {name, version, optional}. A .sigmf archive is a POSIX tar. A .sigmf-collection groups recordings and references each one by the SHA512 of its .sigmf-meta. Because a box is a sample range plus RF edges, it is independent of FFT size, overlap and tile layout. Tiles at any resolution can then be regenerated from the IQ without re-labelling.
    - **Versions and platform:** Spec v1.2.6 (Oct 2026). Plain JSON, platform-independent.
    - **Limits and risks:** core:label is a short free string with no taxonomy. Put the class hierarchy and provenance in your own extension namespace. A box must be axis-aligned, so a Doppler-sloped carrier gets a loose box: store the measured centre-frequency track in the extension, or split long passes into short boxes of about 5-10 s. The global sha512 has to be recomputed whenever the data file changes.
    - **Sources:**
      - https://sigmf.org/
  2.
    - **Name:** SigMF 'signal' extension v1.0.0 (signal:detail only)
    - **Role:** Standard place for the modulation family and protocol of each box
    - **Details:** Verified fields in signal:detail: type, mod_class, standard, carrier_variant, symbol_variant, order, duplexing, multiplexing, multiple_access, spreading, channel_bw, channel, class_variant. The mod_class enumeration is am, fm, pm, ssb, dsb, vsb, ask, fsk, psk, qam, ook, cpm, msk. OFDM is not a mod_class; it goes under multiplexing. The extension also defines signal:emitter (seid, label, manufacturer, power_tx, power_eirp, geolocation).
    - **Versions and platform:** v1.0.0
    - **Limits and risks:** The examples in the spec use 'bandwidth' and 'system', which are not in the table. Do not use signal:emitter: emitter identity and location are out of scope (rules) and a privacy liability. The multiplexing enumeration was not checked.
    - **Sources:**
      - https://raw.githubusercontent.com/sigmf/SigMF/main/extensions/signal.sigmf-ext.md
  3.
    - **Name:** sigmf-python
    - **Role:** Library used to write and read recordings and annotations on the device and on the PC
    - **Details:** Verified from pyproject.toml and sigmffile.py: the package is SigMF, LGPLv3+, requires Python 3.10 or later, and depends on numpy, jsonschema and defusedxml. It installs the console scripts sigmf_validate and sigmf_convert. API: SigMFFile.add_annotation(start_index, length=None, metadata=None) re-sorts the list by sample_start after each add. Other calls are add_capture(start_index, metadata=None), get_annotations(index=None), tofile(file_path, pretty=True, toarchive=False, compression=None, skip_validate=False, overwrite=False), archive(...), validate(), calculate_hash(), read_samples(start_index=0, count=-1) and module-level fromfile(filename, skip_checksum=False, autoscale=True). Data files are memory-mapped with np.memmap, read-only by default, so cutting snippets from multi-GB snapshots does not load them into RAM.
    - **Versions and platform:** Pure Python. Python 3.12 on Ubuntu 24.04 aarch64 meets the >=3.10 requirement. The exact release number was not obtained because the PyPI page did not render.
    - **Limits and risks:** fromfile verifies the checksum by default, which means hashing the whole file. On 1-10 GB snapshots on the T7, pass skip_checksum=True during interactive labelling and verify in a background job instead. Using an LGPL library from your own code is fine.
    - **Sources:**
      - https://raw.githubusercontent.com/sigmf/sigmf-python/main/pyproject.toml
      - https://raw.githubusercontent.com/sigmf/sigmf-python/main/sigmffile.py
  4.
    - **Name:** Snapshot recorder (own component) on the existing RAM ring
    - **Role:** Turns 'I just saw something on the waterfall' into a SigMF recording that can be labelled
    - **Details:** The audited storage plan already has an 8 GiB mlocked RAM ring, with wideband captures going to a Samsung T7 and narrowband passes to the UFS. Computed hold times for that ring: 38.3 s at 56 Msps ci16, 76.7 s at 56 Msps ci8, and about 30 min at RTL 2.4 Msps cu8. A 'Snap' action therefore works as a pre-trigger: it writes the last N seconds, which the user has already seen scroll past. Write ci16 for snapshots of 10 s or less, because 8 bits loses dynamic range next to strong LTE/FM; write ci8 for longer surveys. Write cu8 natively for the RTL-SDR. Per capture, record core:datetime (GNSS/NMEA-disciplined; the audit says SDR buffers are host-stamped at the millisecond level), core:frequency, gain, the SDR model, and a session LO ppm estimate (see AIS-catcher and band-plan calibration). The recorder runs in the capture process. Labelling and auto-labelling run elsewhere, so they can never stall RX.
    - **Versions and platform:** C++ or Python writer with SoapySDR/LimeSuiteNG CS16, consistent with the audited recorder design (named pipe or mbuffer, or a custom mlocked ring). Q6A, Ubuntu 24.04.
    - **Limits and risks:** At 56 Msps the T7 must sustain 112-224 MB/s while RX runs. The audit has a single Q6A USB3 data point (about 395 MB/s fio), with no sustained run. A cs8 snapshot clips when a strong in-band carrier is present. Snap must copy out of the ring without blocking the writer.
    - **Sources:**
      - /tmp/claude-0/-home-user-lizbeth307/f89a86b4-fa51-5ce8-96da-e73d5f771cf3/scratchpad/final/storage.json
      - /tmp/claude-0/-home-user-lizbeth307/f89a86b4-fa51-5ce8-96da-e73d5f771cf3/scratchpad/final/digest.md
  5.
    - **Name:** Pass prediction: CelesTrak OMM + Skyfield + SatNOGS DB transmitters
    - **Role:** Auto-labelling stage 1: predicts boxes for satellite signals in the captured span
    - **Details:** The SatNOGS DB API is public (GET) and has endpoints for transmitters, satellites, modes, tle, telemetry, artifacts, optical-observations and transmitter-params-schemas. Verified transmitter fields: uuid, description, alive, type, downlink_low, downlink_high, downlink_drift, mode, mode_id, baud, norad_cat_id, status, service, frequency_violation, unconfirmed. For Meteor-M2-3 (NORAD 57166) it returns LRPT 137.9/137.1 MHz at 72k and 80k, HRPT 1700 MHz 'BPSK' at 800000 baud, S-band 3405.235 MHz and others. The /api/modes list has 61 entries, among them AFSK, BPSK, CW, DVB-S2, FSK AX.25 G3RUH, GFSK, GMSK, HRPT, LRPT, LoRa, MSK, OQPSK, QPSK, SSTV and FMN. Licence: 'All data are public and freely distributed under the Creative Commons Atribution-Share Alike v4.0 license.' Method: compute Skyfield passes from CelesTrak OMM; the audit already uses EarthSatellite.from_omm because it has no 5-digit NORAD limit. For each alive, active transmitter whose downlink falls inside the SDR span, predict f(t) = f0(1 - range_rate/c). The predicted box is AOS-LOS above the minimum elevation, f(t) +/- (BW_mode(baud)/2 + ppm*f + margin). Doppler bounds, computed for zenith passes and ignoring Earth rotation: 137.9 MHz +/-3.0 kHz and <=31 Hz/s; 437 MHz on the ISS +/-10.5 kHz and <=204 Hz/s; 1.7 GHz +/-37 kHz and <=383 Hz/s; 2.2 GHz +/-50 kHz and <=591 Hz/s.
    - **Versions and platform:** REST and JSON, called from Python on the device. Cache it. The device is offline in the field, so refresh the transmitter list and OMM when there is a network.
    - **Limits and risks:** DB entries can be stale or rough. Meteor HRPT appears as 'BPSK' at 800000 baud, and SatDump's pipeline should be treated as the authority. Use the DB to propose boxes, not to confirm them. The /api/tle endpoint is public, but its TLEs carry tle_source 'Space-Track.org'; Space-Track redistribution terms were not checked, so prefer CelesTrak OMM. /api/artifacts returned HTTP 401 (it needs an API token). The CelesTrak rate-limit policy was not checked here.
    - **Sources:**
      - https://db.satnogs.org/api/
      - https://db.satnogs.org/api/transmitters/?format=json&satellite__norad_cat_id=57166
      - https://db.satnogs.org/api/modes/?format=json
      - https://db.satnogs.org/about/
      - https://db.satnogs.org/api/tle/?format=json&norad_cat_id=57166
  6.
    - **Name:** SatNOGS Network observations (external, weakly labelled waterfalls)
    - **Role:** Extra pretraining and evaluation data for satellite classes from many stations
    - **Details:** Each observation record has start/end, transmitter_uuid, mode and baud, waterfall (PNG URL), payload (OGG audio), demoddata (decoded files), status (for example 'good'), waterfall_status, max_altitude, and client_metadata giving the SDR and sample rate (for example rtlsdr at 1.024 Msps). Licence: 'Observation data are freely distributed under the CC BY-SA license.' A record with demoddata present and status good is a weak positive (the signal is present somewhere in the waterfall); waterfall_status gives a signal or no-signal flag where it has been vetted.
    - **Versions and platform:** Public REST at network.satnogs.org/api/observations. Training-host side only, not the device.
    - **Limits and risks:** No box labels, only presence per observation. Waterfalls are rendered PNGs whose pixel-to-Hz/s mapping, colour scale and Doppler handling were NOT checked, so there is a domain gap against the device's own tiles. Use them for pretraining or weak supervision only, never as test data. CC BY-SA means any redistributed derived dataset is share-alike, and attribution is required.
    - **Sources:**
      - https://network.satnogs.org/about/
      - https://network.satnogs.org/api/observations/
  7.
    - **Name:** gr-satellites as decoder oracle for CubeSat AFSK/GMSK/FSK/BPSK
    - **Role:** Auto-labelling stage 3: ground truth that a predicted or detected box really is the named satellite and mode
    - **Details:** Verified CLI: inputs --wavfile, --rawfile (float32/complex64), --rawint16, --sigmf SIGMF, --udp, --iq, --samp_rate, --start_time, --throttle. Outputs --kiss_out, --kiss_append, --hexdump, --telemetry_output, --kiss_server, --zmq_pub, plus --syncword_threshold (default 8) and --verbose_rs. KISS files store a UNIX-ms timestamp before each frame. For recordings, that timestamp is only meaningful with --throttle plus --start_time (1x replay). Licence GPL-3.0; the v5.x series is current, and the audit runs apt 5.5.0. For a sample-accurate box time, do not rely on those timestamps. Cut the channelised recording into energy-detected bursts or 2-5 s segments, decode each segment, and mark the segment 'decoded' if it yields at least one frame. Store only frame counts, never payloads.
    - **Versions and platform:** gr-satellites 5.5.0 (Ubuntu apt per the audit) on GNU Radio 3.10.9.2, aarch64.
    - **Limits and risks:** How CRC-failed frames are treated is not documented. Test with known recordings to check whether the output means CRC-passed. The docs do not mention sample-index metadata. The tool can run faster than real time offline, but CPU use on A55 cores at about 25-50 kS/s per channel was not measured.
    - **Sources:**
      - https://gr-satellites.readthedocs.io/en/latest/command_line.html
      - https://github.com/daniestevez/gr-satellites
  8.
    - **Name:** SatDump as decoder oracle for Meteor LRPT, NOAA/Meteor HRPT and MetOp AHRPT
    - **Role:** Auto-labelling stage 3 for weather-satellite boxes
    - **Details:** Verified offline syntax: 'satdump pipeline [pipeline_id] [input_level] [input_file] <out_dir> --samplerate 6e6 --baseband_format cs16'. Recording formats are cf32, cs32, cs16, cs8, cu8 and w16; ZIQ needs libzstd. Method: run the pipeline on the whole pass, then repeat on fixed-length segments (for example 10 s). Mark a segment 'decoded' if it produces non-zero CADU output. This avoids parsing log formats. The resulting decoded intervals become the time edges of the box, with the frequency edges taken from the measured spectrum.
    - **Versions and platform:** SatDump master (2.0 alpha) built from source on aarch64, per the audit.
    - **Limits and risks:** The docs page did not list output file names or a machine-readable sync/lock status. That CADU files exist per segment is an assumption to check on one pass. Short segments lose the demodulator lock-in time, so begin each segment about 1-2 s earlier than the interval you label. SigMF input is not mentioned, so pass the .sigmf-data path with --baseband_format and --samplerate.
    - **Sources:**
      - https://docs.satdump.org/
  9.
    - **Name:** dump1090-fa for ADS-B auto-labels at exact sample positions
    - **Role:** Ground truth for 1090 MHz Mode S/ADS-B bursts
    - **Details:** Verified in sdr_ifile.c: --ifile <path> ('-' for stdin), --iformat UC8|SC16|SC16Q11 (default UC8), --throttle. File timestamps come from the sample counter: sampleTimestamp = sampleCounter*12e6/sample_rate. A decoded message's 12 MHz timestamp therefore maps back to the exact sample index. That gives box start = index, length 64 us (short) or 120 us (long, including the 8 us preamble), at 1090 MHz +/- about 1 MHz. Decimate the wideband snapshot to dump1090's rate around 1090 MHz first. Licence GPL-2.0 or later.
    - **Versions and platform:** Builds on aarch64 (Debian packaging in the repo). The exact release was not obtained.
    - **Limits and risks:** Whether the supported sample rates include anything beyond the default 2.4 Msps was not checked. At 56 Msps a 4096-point FFT row lasts 73 us, so an ADS-B burst covers only 1-2 rows and needs a fine-time tiling profile. Decoded ICAO addresses and positions must be discarded (privacy).
    - **Sources:**
      - https://raw.githubusercontent.com/flightaware/dump1090/master/sdr_ifile.c
      - https://github.com/flightaware/dump1090
  10.
    - **Name:** AIS-catcher for AIS auto-labels and LO ppm calibration
    - **Role:** Ground truth for 161.975/162.025 MHz GMSK bursts, and a free frequency-error estimate
    - **Details:** Verified: file input is '-r [format] filename'; formats include CU8 (default) and CS16; the rate is set with -s (integer Hz, 0 to 20,000,000, default 1536K). JSON fields: rxtime and rxuxtime (with -M T) come from the local clock at decode time; signalpower (dB) and ppm, the 'estimated frequency offset of the receiver during decoding' (with -M D); channel A/B. No sample-position field exists; 'toa' is filled only when the input carries an upstream time. Method: energy-detect bursts in about 26.7 ms slots, decode each burst separately (decoded means label 'ais'), and keep the median ppm as the session LO correction. Licence GPL-3.0.
    - **Versions and platform:** Linux, RTL-SDR Blog v4 listed as supported. The aarch64 build was not checked on the Q6A.
    - **Limits and risks:** rxtime is the wall clock at decode time and cannot place a box in a recording, so localise by burst. MMSI, positions and names must never be stored.
    - **Sources:**
      - https://jvde-github.github.io/AIS-catcher-docs/configuration/input/file/
      - https://jvde-github.github.io/AIS-catcher-docs/references/JSON-decoding/
      - https://github.com/jvde-github/AIS-catcher
  11.
    - **Name:** radiosonde_auto_rx and band-plan rules for the other classes
    - **Role:** Auto-label sources for radiosonde, broadcast FM, cellular, ISM, DVB-S2, SSTV, APRS and CW
    - **Details:** radiosonde_auto_rx is GPL-3.0 and supports RS41, RS92, DFM, M10/M20, iMet-4/54, LMS6, iMS-100, MRZ-H1, MTS01 and others. It is documented for live RTL-SDR/AirSpy use; file input is unconfirmed, so run it live in parallel only when it can own a separate SDR. For everything else use rule-based weak labels plus human confirmation. Broadcast FM: 87.5-108 MHz carriers about 200 kHz wide. GSM/LTE downlink: national band-plan blocks with the typical spectral shapes (200 kHz bursts in a TDMA frame; flat OFDM blocks of 1.4-20 MHz). Wi-Fi: about 20 MHz OFDM bursts on the 2.4 GHz channel grid. BLE/BT: about 1-2 MHz short hopping bursts. DVB-S2: QO-100 wideband beacon at the LNB IF. SSTV: ARISS event schedule at 145.800 MHz. APRS: 144.800 MHz, the Region 1 frequency (assumption). CW: SatNOGS 'CW' transmitters, confirmed by an OOK on/off pattern without decoding.
    - **Versions and platform:** Rules in Python on the device or PC. Tools such as Direwolf, redsea (RDS), kalibrate (FCCH) and LTE cell search could serve as presence-only confirmers, but none of them was checked in this pass.
    - **Limits and risks:** Band-plan labels are weak (tier 'predicted'). The national allocations for Ukraine were not checked. 2400-2483.5 MHz (83.5 MHz) does not fit in one 56 MHz LimeSDR span. The LimeSDR Micro does not ship until 15 Dec 2026, so all 1.766-3.8 GHz data waits until then. Cellular and ISM signals are labelled only as interference classes; no cell, network or device identities are decoded.
    - **Sources:**
      - https://github.com/projecthorus/radiosonde_auto_rx
  12.
    - **Name:** Touch labelling UI: SDR++ module overlay for live use, plus a separate snapshot labeller
    - **Role:** Lets the user draw a box on the waterfall with a finger and pick a class
    - **Details:** Verified in SDR++'s frequency_manager source: a module can bind gui::waterfall.onFFTRedraw (FFTRedrawArgs gives min/max screen coords, lowFreq, highFreq, freqToPixelRatio and a DrawList) and gui::waterfall.onInputProcess (it can claim clicks with inputHandled = true). Frequency maps to x as x = min.x + (f - lowFreq)*freqToPixelRatio. That is enough for a live module that draws detector and auto-label markers and offers a 'Snap/Label' button. Box drawing itself belongs in a frozen snapshot view, because a finger cannot track a scrolling waterfall. That view should be a separate full-screen app, for example a Chromium-kiosk page with Pointer Events for pinch and pan, plus a local Python backend that renders tiles from the memmapped SigMF. Display maths for the audited 7 in 1920x1080 panel: 314.7 PPI, 12.4 px/mm, so a 9 mm touch target is about 112 px. IQEngine (MIT) is a SigMF spectrogram viewer and editor that can add annotations 'graphically or through text' and visualise local files client-side; it suits review on the PC.
    - **Versions and platform:** SDR++ built from source on aarch64 per the audit, running under the cage kiosk. IQEngine is a web app (Docker files in the repo).
    - **Limits and risks:** Not checked: whether SDR++ exposes a redraw hook for the waterfall region (frequency_manager draws in the FFT area), and how waterfall rows map to time. Also not checked: whether IQEngine saves edited annotations back to .sigmf-meta, and its touch behaviour and performance on the Q6A. ImGui has no native pinch gestures (unverified), which is a reason to build the labeller outside SDR++. Finger boxes are imprecise, so snap-to-signal refinement is needed.
    - **Sources:**
      - https://raw.githubusercontent.com/AlexandreRouma/SDRPlusPlus/master/misc_modules/frequency_manager/src/main.cpp
      - https://github.com/IQEngine/IQEngine
      - https://raw.githubusercontent.com/IQEngine/IQEngine/main/README.md
  13.
    - **Name:** Dataset versioning: DVC on the PC, a content-addressed manifest on the device
    - **Role:** Reproducible dataset versions, each tied to model versions
    - **Details:** DVC is Apache-2.0, public and maintained; no archival or ownership notice was seen in Oct 2026. On the device, keep an append-only store: each recording is a .sigmf-meta/.sigmf-data pair named by its sha512 (core:sha512). Annotation edits create a new meta revision. A JSONL or Parquet manifest records recording hash, meta hash, session_id, pass_id, SDR, class counts, label tiers, licence and privacy class. On the PC, the dataset is a DVC-tracked manifest plus taxonomy.yaml (semver) plus tiling.yaml (FFT size, window, overlap, dB normalisation) plus splits.json. Every model artifact records the dataset version hash, so a new signal class means a new taxonomy minor version and a new dataset version.
    - **Versions and platform:** DVC (pip) on the x86-64 Ubuntu 22.04 training host. The device needs only Python and sha512sum.
    - **Limits and risks:** DVC's release number was not obtained. Do not run DVC on the device: there is no benefit and it adds git and cache overhead. Moving data by T7 swap needs a manifest-diff import step.
    - **Sources:**
      - https://github.com/iterative/dvc
      - https://sigmf.org/
  14.
    - **Name:** TorchSig transforms and synthetic wideband scenes
    - **Role:** Augmentation and synthetic pretraining with exact box labels
    - **Details:** TorchSig is MIT, needs Python 3.10 or later and Ubuntu 22.04 or later, and claims support for '60+ signal types' (FSK, QAM, PSK, ASK, OFDM, analog). Its unified dataset handles detection when num_signals_max > 1. Verified classes in transforms.py: AWGN, AdditiveNoise, TimeVaryingNoise, AdjacentChannelInterference, CochannelInterference, CarrierFrequencyDrift (ppm), CarrierPhaseNoise, CarrierPhaseOffset, ClockDrift, ClockJitter, CoarseGainChange, DigitalAGC, Doppler, Fading (Rayleigh tapped FIR only, no Rician), IntermodulationProducts, IQImbalance (including DC offset), NonlinearAmplifier, PassbandRipple, Quantize, RandomDropSamples, Shadowing, SpectralInversion, Spurs, CutOut, PatchShuffle, TimeReversal, Spectrogram, SpectrogramDropSamples, SpectrogramImage, ChannelSwap. There is no dedicated frequency-shift, resample or time-shift class, so write those with numpy/scipy (complex mixer, resample_poly) and their box bookkeeping. The WBSig53 work (arXiv 2211.10335, per search results) used 512x512 spectrograms with 53 classes and YOLO-style (xc, yc, w, h) boxes.
    - **Versions and platform:** Training host (x86-64). The release number was not shown on GitHub; a GRCon 2025 paper 'TorchSig 2.0' exists.
    - **Limits and risks:** Not checked: a YOLO export, and whether the Doppler transform models time-varying LEO ramps (its description says it 'updates center frequency and bandwidth'). Synthetic waveforms are generic families, not LRPT/AIS/ADS-B protocol-exact, so pretrain on them and fine-tune on real device data. Some transforms (TimeReversal, SpectralInversion) create physically impossible satellite tracks; use them sparingly or not at all.
    - **Sources:**
      - https://github.com/TorchDSP/torchsig
      - https://raw.githubusercontent.com/TorchDSP/torchsig/main/torchsig/transforms/transforms.py
      - https://arxiv.org/pdf/2211.10335
  15.
    - **Name:** External datasets and their licences
    - **Role:** Supplements to the user's own data
    - **Details:** DeepSig RadioML 2016.04C, 2016.10A and 2018.01A: 'licensed under the Creative Commons Attribution - NonCommercial - ShareAlike 4.0 License'. DeepSig says they have 'several known errata', are 'NOT currently used within DeepSig products', and recommends building datasets from real data. 2018.01A has 24 classes, 2M examples of 1024 samples, HDF5. These are IQ-snippet classification sets with no boxes. Fraunhofer EAS Wi-Fi/Bluetooth spectrogram frame-detection set: 20,000 augmented segments with frame position and type labels, CC BY 4.0 according to the MDPI listing (DOI 10.3390/data7120168); it is synthetic mixing of generated frames. Wood et al. 2022 (arXiv 2210.16173) published a spectrogram object-detection dataset (RetinaNet and YOLOv5, mAP up to 0.906); its data licence was not stated on the abstract page. SatNOGS DB and Network: CC BY-SA.
    - **Versions and platform:** Used on the PC only.
    - **Limits and risks:** RadioML is NC plus SA: keep it out of any model or dataset that may be shared commercially, and treat models trained on it as possibly derivative (legal interpretation unverified). The Fraunhofer licence was not confirmed on the repository page (MDPI returned 403). Do not use RF-fingerprinting or emitter-ID sets.
    - **Sources:**
      - https://www.deepsig.ai/datasets/
      - https://ideas.repec.org/a/gam/jdataj/v7y2022i12p168-d981986.html
      - https://www.mdpi.com/2306-5729/7/12/168
      - https://arxiv.org/abs/2210.16173
- **Recommendations:**
  - 1. Store labels in physical units, not pixels. One SigMF v1.2.6 recording per snapshot or pass. Each box is sample_start/sample_count plus RF freq_lower_edge/freq_upper_edge in Hz, with a short core:label of 20 characters or fewer (e.g. lrpt, hrpt, ahrpt, aprs1200, cs_gmsk, cs_fsk, bpsk_tlm, cw, nfm_voice, sstv, adsb, ais, sonde, dvbs2, lte_dl, gsm_dl, wifi, ble_bt, bcast_fm, noise, art_dc, art_spur, art_image, unknown). Declare an optional extension 'rflab' v0.1.0 in core:extensions, with class_path (family/protocol), tier (decoded | predicted | human | model), verified, score, decoder@version, n_frames_ok, transmitter_uuid and norad_id (public satellites only), pass_id, session_id, snr_db, ppm_est and privacy_class. Put signal:detail.mod_class/standard where known, and never use signal:emitter. Tiles are always regenerated from IQ with a versioned tiling.yaml, so a change of FFT size, overlap or dB scaling never needs relabelling. YOLO conversion per tile: xc = ((f_lo+f_hi)/2 - (fc - fs/2))/fs; w = (f_hi - f_lo)/fs; yc = (sample_start + sample_count/2 - s0)/(rows*hop); h = sample_count/(rows*hop). Clip to the tile. Drop boxes under 2 px or that keep under 50% of their area, and mark them as ignore regions.
  - 2. Collection modes. (a) 'Snap': dump the last N s of the 8 GiB RAM ring to SigMF on the T7: 4 s at 56 Msps ci8 (448 MB) or 10 s ci16 for spans of 20 MHz or less, and 30-120 s cu8 for the RTL. (b) 'Pass': the scheduler records the predicted channel or span from AOS to LOS. (c) 'Survey': the detector-gated ring commits only segments that contain detections, which also protects the UFS from wear. Stamp core:datetime from the GNSS-disciplined clock and store the session ppm, estimated from the AIS-catcher ppm median or from known broadcast or beacon carriers. The V4L's 1 ppm TCXO is +/-1.7 kHz at 1.7 GHz and +/-137 Hz at 137.9 MHz.
  - 3. Auto-labelling pipeline, run after capture as a niced job off the RX cores and never live on the RX path. PREDICT: Skyfield on CelesTrak OMM plus cached SatNOGS DB transmitters (alive, status=active) give Doppler-curved candidate windows; band-plan rules cover terrestrial classes. DETECT: a CFAR/energy detector inside each window turns detections into tight boxes, one per burst or packet, and 5-10 s slices for continuous carriers. DOPPLER TEST: fit the measured centre-frequency track to the predicted curve with a free constant offset. Accept as 'predicted' if the residual RMS is under about 1 kHz (UHF) or 3 kHz (L-band). This also rejects terrestrial signals on the same frequency, whose track is flat. CONFIRM: decoders run on channelised segments. gr_satellites uses --sigmf or --rawfile --samp_rate, plus --kiss_out. SatDump runs 'satdump pipeline <id> baseband <seg> <out> --samplerate --baseband_format'. dump1090-fa uses --ifile --iformat, with sample index = ts*fs/12e6. AIS-catcher uses -r CS16 file -s rate -M D, decoding each burst separately. A segment with at least one valid frame or CADU becomes tier 'decoded'. Never place boxes from wall-clock decoder times (AIS rxtime, gr-satellites KISS ms); localise by segment or burst instead.
  - 4. Label tiers and how training uses them. 'decoded' and 'human' are ground truth with weight 1. 'predicted' gets weight 0.5, or ground truth only after review. 'model' (detector proposals) is never ground truth until accepted. Energy-only detections with no prediction go to the review queue as 'unknown'. Background tiles count as 'noise' only when no prediction, no detection and no proposal touches them; this is a hard-negative pool that includes RTL/Lime artifacts (DC/LO leakage, spurs, IQ images, FM-overload intermod), which get their own art_* classes so the detector stops firing on them.
  - 5. Touch UI. The live SDR++ module draws boxes from the detector and auto-labeller as colour-coded outlines (dashed = unverified) and has one large 'Snap and label' button; it uses onFFTRedraw and onInputProcess, which are verified in frequency_manager. The labeller is a separate full-screen kiosk app on the frozen snapshot. Drag to draw, then snap-to-signal: within the finger box plus 20% margin, threshold at the median noise + 6 dB per bin and take the bounding box of the largest connected component. Pinch and pan to zoom (time and frequency independently), with handles and hit zones of at least 112 px (9 mm at 315 PPI). The class picker is a grid of large buttons sorted by: (i) the SatNOGS or band-plan prediction at that time and frequency, (ii) the model's top 3, (iii) the user's recent picks, and (iv) 'unknown' and 'artifact'. One-swipe accept or reject for each proposal, plus undo. Show the predicted Doppler curve as an overlay. There is no audio-demodulation button anywhere.
  - 6. Active-learning review queue. Order items by (a) model score 0.3-0.7, (b) disagreement between model and auto-label, (c) classes under target count, and (d) a new site, SDR or gain. Aim for review sessions of about 5 minutes of 20-40 items. Keep a small blind audit set, labelled without proposals shown, to measure how far the user's labels drift toward the model's suggestions.
  - 7. Splits, with no leakage. Split by group, never by tile. The group is the pass_id for satellites and the session_id (snapshot or day) for terrestrial data. Use StratifiedGroupKFold-style assignment at about 70/15/15. Keep whole days, and where possible a different site or antenna, in the test set. Freeze test-set membership by recording hash so that adding data never moves test items.
  - 8. Balancing. Cap each group's contribution per class (e.g. 50 boxes per pass per class) so that one long LRPT pass or one busy LTE band does not dominate. Use class-aware sampling. Keep about 20-30% of training tiles as background or hard negatives. Rare classes (SSTV events, radiosondes, DVB-S2, HRPT) are boosted with copy-paste augmentation rather than duplication. Rule of thumb (unverified): at least 300 verified boxes from at least 10 distinct groups before a class is enabled on the NPU.
  - 9. New classes over time. Bump the taxonomy minor version, add the label, harvest examples through the review queue and auto-rules, and retrain. Any class with too few examples maps to 'unknown' in that model version, which keeps old models consistent. The deployment manifest records the taxonomy and dataset hashes, so on-device overlays show 'unknown (v1.3)' rather than a wrong name.
  - 10. Augmentation runs on the PC, in the IQ domain, before the STFT, and every transform updates the boxes. Frequency shift (shift the boxes). Resample with resample_poly, ratio 0.8-1.25 (scale time and bandwidth). LEO Doppler ramps from real Skyfield pass geometry, applied by phase integration with the box re-bounded to the ramp; bounds are +/-3 kHz at 137 MHz up to +/-50 kHz and about 0.6 kHz/s at 2.2 GHz. Rician and Rayleigh fading plus Shadowing. IQImbalance and DC (label the created image as art_image, or mask it). Spurs, CarrierPhaseNoise, ClockDrift, NonlinearAmplifier, IntermodulationProducts, Adjacent and CochannelInterference, AWGN at controlled SNR, and CoarseGainChange or DigitalAGC, all from TorchSig (MIT). Copy-paste: insert channelised labelled snippets into real background captures from the same SDR at random time, frequency and SNR, for dense scenes with exact boxes. After noise or gain augmentation, recompute per-box SNR and convert boxes below about 0 dB in-band SNR into ignore regions instead of positives. Spectrogram-domain extras: dB-offset jitter, SpectrogramDropSamples, and mild FFT-window or size jitter.
  - 11. Retention and storage. Raw wideband snapshots are kept on the T7 for 14 days after their labels and tiles have been extracted, then deleted unless pinned. Transient pass channel files are deleted after the decoder oracle has run. Snippets and tiles are kept permanently: on the UFS up to an assigned quota (e.g. 20 GB of the 128 GB), then mirrored to the T7 or PC. Each box keeps a channelised ci16 snippet at 1.25x its bandwidth (minimum 25 kS/s), capped at 1 s (0.25 s for voice-capable classes), plus one 512x512 uint8 context tile (262 kB).
  - 12. Privacy rules, enforced in code. Decoders are confirmation oracles only. They run sandboxed (systemd-run with PrivateNetwork=yes and a read-only input), and a wrapper passes on only {ok, n_frames, crc_rate, snr, ppm}. Payloads, ICAO addresses, MMSIs, callsigns, positions, RDS PS and cell IDs are discarded and never written. There is no audio demodulation in the labeller. Voice-capable classes (nfm_voice, AM, SSB) get IQ snippets of 0.25 s or less, or spectrogram tiles only at detector resolution. Exported datasets round geolocation to about 0.1 degree or a 4-character Maidenhead locator; the exact position stays on the device for pass prediction. The LimeSDR TX path stays disabled. Synthetic waveforms are generated in software only and never transmitted.
  - 13. Licences per record. Store the licence and source in the rflab extension and in the manifest: own captures (yours), SatNOGS-derived (CC BY-SA 4.0, attribution plus share-alike), TorchSig-generated (MIT code; generated data yours), Fraunhofer Wi-Fi/BT (CC BY 4.0, unverified on the repository), RadioML (CC BY-NC-SA 4.0). Build a 'redistributable' dataset view that excludes NC data. Decoder tools (GPL-2.0+ or GPL-3.0) run as separate processes and do not affect the dataset's licence.
- **Numbers:**
  - Raw IQ per hour: LimeSDR 56 Msps ci16 = 224 MB/s = 806 GB/h; ci8 = 403 GB/h; 61.44 Msps ci16 = 885 GB/h; 7 Msps ci16 = 101 GB/h; RTL-SDR 2.4 Msps cu8 = 17.3 GB/h; 2.56 Msps = 18.4 GB/h; 1.024 Msps = 7.4 GB/h
  - 8 GiB RAM ring hold time: 38.3 s at 56 Msps ci16, 76.7 s at 56 Msps ci8, about 30 min at 2.4 Msps cu8
  - uint8 dB spectrogram archive: 56 Msps with 4096 bins (13.67 kHz/bin) at 1 ms rows = 4.1 MB/s = 14.7 GB/h; at 10 ms rows = 1.47 GB/h; 8192 bins at 10 ms = 2.95 GB/h; RTL 2.4 Msps with 1024 bins (2.34 kHz) at 10 ms = 0.37 GB/h; 2048 bins at 1 ms = 7.4 GB/h (before compression)
  - Per-box ci16 snippet at 1.25x bandwidth (minimum 25 kS/s): AIS burst (26.7 ms) 3.3 kB; ADS-B long (120 us) 1.2 kB; BLE advertising burst 4 kB; NFM voice capped at 0.25 s = 25 kB; GMSK 9k6 packet (0.5 s) 50 kB; APRS, BPSK, SSTV or sonde (1 s) 100 kB; Wi-Fi 1 ms burst 100 kB; broadcast FM 0.25 s 250 kB; Meteor LRPT 1 s 750 kB; LTE 10 MHz 20 ms 1 MB; DVB-S2 0.1 s 1.35 MB; HRPT 0.25 s 3.4 MB
  - 512x512 uint8 context tile = 262 kB; a SigMF annotation is about 400 B of JSON, so 10k annotations is about 4 MB (estimate)
  - Example hourly budgets: auto-label survey at about 600 boxes/h (snippet plus tile) is about 0.25 GB/h; 12 user snapshots/h of 4 s at 56 Msps ci8 is about 5.4 GB/h (T7); transient pass channel files are about 12 GB/h and deleted after decoding; kept pass snippets about 0.04 GB/h
  - LEO Doppler bounds (zenith pass, no Earth rotation): 137.9 MHz +/-3.0 kHz, <=31 Hz/s; 145.8 MHz ISS +/-3.5 kHz, <=68 Hz/s; 437 MHz ISS +/-10.5 kHz, <=204 Hz/s; 435 MHz at 520 km +/-10.2 kHz, <=161 Hz/s; 1.7 GHz +/-37 kHz, <=383 Hz/s; 2.2 GHz +/-50 kHz, <=591 Hz/s
  - LO error from the RTL-SDR V4L's 1 ppm TCXO: +/-137 Hz at 137.9 MHz, +/-437 Hz at 437 MHz, +/-1.7 kHz at 1.7 GHz; a 1 s clock error is at most about 0.4 kHz of predicted-frequency error at 1.7 GHz
  - Time resolution: at 56 Msps a 4096-point FFT row is 73 us, so ADS-B (64/120 us) spans 1-2 rows and AIS (26.7 ms) about 365 rows
  - Display: 7 in 1920x1080 = 314.7 PPI = 12.4 px/mm, so a 9 mm touch target is about 112 px
  - SigMF spec v1.2.6; label recommended at 20 characters or fewer; signal extension v1.0.0; mod_class has 13 values
  - The SatNOGS DB modes list has 61 entries (Oct 2026); dump1090 file timestamps use a 12 MHz clock (sampleCounter*12e6/fs); AIS-catcher file sample rate goes up to 20,000,000 Hz (default 1536K)
- **Rejected:**
  1.
    - **Name:** Drawing boxes on the live scrolling waterfall
    - **Why:** A finger cannot track a moving image, and the signal has already scrolled away. Pre-trigger snapshots from the RAM ring plus a frozen labeller are reliable.
  2.
    - **Name:** Storing boxes in tile or pixel coordinates (YOLO txt as the master format)
    - **Why:** Labels would be tied to one FFT size, overlap and tile layout. SigMF sample and Hz boxes let tiles for any SDR rate up to 56 Msps be regenerated without relabelling.
  3.
    - **Name:** Recording everything raw at 56 Msps
    - **Why:** That is 806 GB/h at ci16 (403 GB/h at ci8), which fills the 1 TB T7 in about 1.2-2.5 h and breaks the short-snippet privacy goal. Use snapshot, pass and detector-gated capture instead.
  4.
    - **Name:** Random tile-level train/val/test split
    - **Why:** Adjacent tiles from the same pass or snapshot are near-duplicates, so a random split leaks and inflates accuracy. Split by pass or session group, and hold out whole days and sites.
  5.
    - **Name:** Using decoder wall-clock timestamps (AIS-catcher rxtime, gr-satellites KISS ms) to place boxes in recordings
    - **Why:** Both come from the local clock at decode time (verified), not from the sample position. Use dump1090's sample-counter timestamps, or burst- and segment-wise decoding.
  6.
    - **Name:** SatNOGS DB /api/tle as the orbit source
    - **Why:** Its TLEs come from Space-Track.org (redistribution terms unverified). CelesTrak OMM with Skyfield is already the audited choice. /api/artifacts also needs authentication (HTTP 401).
  7.
    - **Name:** RadioML 2016/2018 as the core training set
    - **Why:** CC BY-NC-SA 4.0 with known errata, and DeepSig itself no longer uses it. It is 1024-sample IQ classification with no time-frequency boxes, so at most it is optional pretraining for a second-stage IQ classifier, kept out of any shared model.
  8.
    - **Name:** Generic image annotators (Label Studio, CVAT) as the main labeller
    - **Why:** They lose the physical units and SigMF provenance, and they are not built for pinch-zoomed time-frequency boxes on a 7 in touch screen. Not tested on the Q6A.
  9.
    - **Name:** IQEngine as the on-device labeller
    - **Why:** Its touch support and Q6A performance, and whether it saves annotations to .sigmf-meta, are unverified. It is kept as the PC-side review and visualisation tool (MIT).
  10.
    - **Name:** On-device augmentation or dataset building with DVC on the Q6A
    - **Why:** It takes CPU from RX and DSP and gives nothing over doing the work on the training host. The device keeps only an append-only, sha512-addressed SigMF store and manifest.
  11.
    - **Name:** Classes for drones and FPV links, EW or jammers, radar, or military emitters, and RF-fingerprinting or emitter-ID datasets (signal:emitter, ORACLE-style sets)
    - **Why:** Excluded by the project rules and dual-use in the user's region. Wideband interference is labelled only as generic 'unknown' or 'art_*', never by emitter.
  12.
    - **Name:** Storing decoded content (audio, APRS, ADS-B or AIS identities and positions, RDS, cell IDs)
    - **Why:** Privacy rule. Decoders serve only as yes/no oracles, and their payloads are discarded inside a sandbox.
  13.
    - **Name:** TimeReversal and SpectralInversion as default augmentations
    - **Why:** They produce physically impossible Doppler tracks and mirrored protocol signatures, which hurts detection of satellite S-curves. Use them rarely, if at all.
- **Open questions:**
  - Does SDR++ expose a redraw or input hook for the waterfall region (not only the FFT area used by frequency_manager), and how do waterfall rows map to sample time? This decides whether live box overlays can live inside SDR++.
  - Does SatDump write a machine-readable sync/lock or CADU count per run that can be parsed reliably? Check on one recorded LRPT and one HRPT pass that segment-wise decoding marks the right intervals.
  - Does gr-satellites output only CRC-valid frames for each decoder, and does its --sigmf input honour captures and annotations? Test with known recordings.
  - What exactly do SatNOGS Network waterfall PNGs contain (pixel-to-Hz and time scale, dB scale, Doppler-corrected or not, axes or legends)? This decides whether they are usable for weak pretraining.
  - Confirm the Fraunhofer Wi-Fi/BT dataset licence (CC BY 4.0) on the FORDATIS repository page, and the dataset licence for Wood et al. 2022 (arXiv 2210.16173).
  - TorchSig: the current release number, whether it can export YOLO/COCO boxes, and whether its Doppler transform supports time-varying ramps. Otherwise write a custom LEO ramp generator.
  - Legal: rules in Ukraine (including under martial law) on recording, keeping or sharing ADS-B, AIS, voice or cellular snippets. Not researched; keep everything local until checked.
  - LimeSDR Micro DC, LO-leakage and IQ-image levels on this unit (ships 15 Dec 2026), which set how much art_* hard-negative data is needed and whether IQImbalance augmentation should match measured values.
  - Sustained T7 and UFS write while RX and labelling jobs run together, against the 112-224 MB/s snapshot rate (the audit has a single Q6A USB3 data point of about 395 MB/s).
  - How to handle overlapping and co-channel signals (for example LTE plus a weak satellite) in detector training: overlapping boxes, ignore masks, or a segmentation target. This is to be settled together with the detector-model work.
  - How many verified boxes per class are needed for the INT8 HTP detector to be within 2 points of FP32 per class (the audit's acceptance rule)? To be measured; the 300-box and 10-group threshold is only a starting rule of thumb.
- **Notes:** Input audit context comes from /tmp/claude-0/-home-user-lizbeth307/f89a86b4-fa51-5ce8-96da-e73d5f771cf3/scratchpad/final/digest.md, software.json, compute.json and storage.json. Facts used: the 8 GiB mlocked RAM ring, the T7 for wideband and UFS for narrowband, the 1 ppm TCXO on the RTL-SDR V4L at 2.56 Msps stable, GNSS NMEA time with ms-level host stamping, Skyfield from_omm, SatDump built from source, gr-satellites 5.5.0 from apt, and the NPU as an optional INT8 accelerator behind a watchdog. Training, quantisation and the detector architecture are outside this area. This area only guarantees that the data stays tiling-agnostic (physical-unit SigMF boxes) so other stages can pick FFT, overlap and dB settings freely.
  
  Verified by fetch this session: SigMF v1.2.6 fields and rules; signal extension v1.0.0; sigmf-python licence, dependencies and API; TorchSig MIT licence and transform class names; DeepSig licence and caveats; SatNOGS DB endpoints, transmitter fields, 61 modes, CC BY-SA 4.0; SatNOGS Network CC BY-SA; that /api/tle comes from Space-Track and /api/artifacts returns 401; gr-satellites CLI including --sigmf, GPL-3.0; SatDump offline CLI syntax; dump1090 --ifile/--iformat and the 12 MHz sample-counter timestamps, GPL-2.0+; AIS-catcher -r/-s and JSON fields, GPL-3.0; radiosonde_auto_rx GPL-3.0 and its sonde types; DVC Apache-2.0; IQEngine MIT and its annotation editing; SDR++ frequency_manager overlay and input hooks.
  
  Not verified, marked in the text: tool release numbers for TorchSig, DVC and dump1090; the Fraunhofer licence (search snippet only); SatDump output files; gr-satellites CRC behaviour; SatNOGS waterfall format; the national band plans for Ukraine; Direwolf, redsea, kalibrate and LTE-scan behaviour; all rule-of-thumb thresholds (300 boxes, 10 groups, 6 dB snap threshold, Doppler residual limits, 14-day retention), which are design proposals, not measured values.
  
  Doppler and storage numbers were computed in Python here: simple circular-orbit geometry for Doppler, and bytes = rate x bytes-per-sample for storage. The scratchpad folder dl_satnogs also holds observation JSON fetched earlier by another stage; only its field names were used. 4 WebSearch calls were used.

## npu:training_compute (run `wf_62c18130-b0d`)

- **Area:** Where and how to train the spectrogram detector and classifier (Q6A CPU, Adreno GPU, home PC, cloud), on-device few-shot and incremental learning, and the ONNX -> QAIRT 2.42 export path with calibration
- **Findings:**
  1.
    - **Name:** The HTP (Hexagon v68) cannot train; it can only run frozen models
    - **Role:** Defines what 'training the NPU' means. Training runs on the CPU, the base PC or the cloud. The NPU runs the frozen detector and an embedding network, and new classes are learned in a CPU head or as prototypes over NPU outputs.
    - **Details:** Qualcomm's HTP backend doc covers inference and performance configuration only. It documents no backward pass and no on-device training API. Its only weight-update features are Weight Sharing ('Only supports Hexagon v73 and onward') and LoRA weight sharing ('Only supports offline prepare on x86_Linux platform'). Neither helps on v68. The doc says 8- and 16-bit quantized networks run on all SoCs and FP16 only on select SoCs. Radxa users confirm v68 rejects FP16. Online prepare (a DLC finalised on the device by qnn-net-run) exists, so a context binary is not strictly required.
    - **Versions and platform:** QAIRT 2.42.0.251225 runtime (qcom-qnn-sdk-v68) on Radxa OS r2. QCS6490 = dsp_arch v68, soc_id 35 (Radxa qairt-usage page).
    - **Limits and risks:** Every change to weights on the NPU means re-quantising and regenerating the context binary. Keep the parts that change often (class heads, prototypes) off the NPU.
    - **Sources:**
      - https://docs.qualcomm.com/bundle/publicresource/80-63442-10/topics/htp_backend.md
      - https://docs.radxa.com/en/dragon/q6a/app-dev/npu-dev/qairt-usage
      - https://forum.radxa.com/t/dragon-q6a-qnn-htp-pipeline-working-but-int8-only-firmware-blocks-real-ml-workloads/31217
  2.
    - **Name:** On-device CPU training with PyTorch aarch64 (CPU-only wheel)
    - **Role:** Field tiers: training heads and prototypes in seconds, and fine-tuning the small box-crop embedder in minutes. The CPU is not used to train the detector.
    - **Details:** PyPI has torch 2.14.1 (30 Sep 2026) cp310-cp314 manylinux_2_28_aarch64 wheels. The PyPI aarch64 wheel is a CUDA 13 build (454 MB) whose metadata pulls cuda-toolkit 13.0.3, cuDNN, NCCL and triton on Linux, all useless on the Q6A. Install from https://download.pytorch.org/whl/cpu instead: torch-2.14.1+cpu cp312 aarch64 is 159 MB. Also available for cp312 aarch64: torchvision 0.29.1, onnxruntime 1.31.0 (21.4 MB), onnx 1.23.2, scikit-learn 1.9.1 and faiss-cpu 1.15.1. Throughput is derived, not measured. The 4x A78 FP32 peak is about 158 GFLOPS: 16 FLOP/cycle from two 128-bit FMA pipes, at 1x 2.7 GHz + 3x 2.4 GHz. At an assumed 10-25% training efficiency that gives 16-40 GFLOPS. With CPU7 reserved for the LimeSDR RX thread (audit), 3 cores give about 12-29 GFLOPS. Estimates from my analytic MAC count: a 0.3 M-parameter crop embedder (21 MMAC on 1x64x64) fine-tunes at about 3-8 s per epoch on 1000 crops, so 30 epochs take 2-4 min. A linear or cosine head over 128-d embeddings trains in well under 1 s. A YOLOv8n-class detector at 256x256 on 10k tiles takes 18-44 min per epoch, or 29-73 h for 100 epochs, which is not feasible in the field. PowerTrain (arXiv 2407.13944) found the Raspberry Pi 5 (A76) trains on CPU only, about two orders of magnitude slower than a Jetson Orin.
    - **Versions and platform:** Ubuntu 24.04 (Python 3.12) on Radxa OS r2, kernel 6.18.2-4 held. Use a venv, not system pip.
    - **Limits and risks:** Thermal: the board throttles at about 90-91 C without a fan (Tj 95 C), and training is a sustained all-core load. Power draw during training is unverified (estimate +3-6 W; measure it on the 12 V rail). CPU contention can starve the SDR RX and FastRPC threads, so never train during a pass. All timing numbers are estimates and need a benchmark on the board.
    - **Sources:**
      - https://pypi.org/project/torch/2.14.1/
      - https://download.pytorch.org/whl/cpu/torch/
      - https://pypi.org/project/onnxruntime/1.31.0/
      - https://arxiv.org/abs/2407.13944
  3.
    - **Name:** Adreno 643 GPU training paths: none usable in production in Oct 2026
    - **Role:** Checks whether the GPU could take over training from the CPU. Conclusion: keep the GPU for the waterfall and FFT, not for training.
    - **Details:** Turnip Vulkan compute works: vkpeak gives 808 GFLOPS FP32 / 1581 FP16, and clpeak gives Vulkan 1096/748, Qualcomm OpenCL 943/650 and rusticl 405/553 (Radxa forum, from the audit). Framework status: (1) Burn (Rust) supports autodiff on its CubeCL Vulkan backend, and its README lists Qualcomm under Vulkan. It is untested on Turnip/A643, and training code would have to be rewritten in Rust. (2) MNN advertises on-device training (MNN-Train) and Vulkan/OpenCL inference backends. Whether backward passes run on its GPU backends is unverified. (3) tinygrad's QCOM backend (Adreno 6xx) drives the KGSL kernel driver directly (ops_qcom.py imports kgsl). Radxa OS uses upstream msm/Freedreno, so /dev/kgsl-3d0 is probably absent (check with ls /dev/kgsl*). tinygrad's CL backend on rusticl is slow. (4) ncnn is inference-only. (5) ExecuTorch's Vulkan delegate supports FP32/FP16 inference modes, and ExecuTorch training is 'experimental', with delegate integration still a work in progress. (6) PyTorch's Vulkan workflow tutorial now returns 404.
    - **Versions and platform:** Mesa 25.2.8 Turnip on Radxa OS r2. Burn main branch (Oct 2026). tinygrad master.
    - **Limits and risks:** The theoretical 5-10x gain over the CPU matters only for jobs this design does not run on the device (full detector training). Heads and the embedder finish in minutes on the CPU anyway.
    - **Sources:**
      - https://github.com/tracel-ai/burn
      - https://github.com/tinygrad/tinygrad/blob/master/docs/runtime.md
      - https://github.com/tinygrad/tinygrad/blob/master/tinygrad/runtime/ops_qcom.py
      - https://github.com/alibaba/MNN

  6.
    - **Name:** Field few-shot learning: frozen NPU embedder + imprinted prototypes + CPU cosine head
    - **Role:** Lets the user teach a new signal by marking 5-20 boxes on the waterfall, with no retraining or reconversion.
    - **Details:** Two-stage pipeline. (1) The NPU detector finds boxes. (2) Each box is cropped from the dB spectrogram with about 25% margin and resized to 1x64x64. A frozen embedder (about 0.3 M parameters, 21 MMAC, INT8 on HTP or FP32 on ORT CPU) produces a 128-d vector, and the CPU L2-normalises it in FP32. Box scalars are appended: log bandwidth, log duration, band and duty cycle. A new class's prototype is the mean of its normalised embeddings ('imprinted weights', Qi/Brown/Lowe, CVPR 2018: averaging beats nearest-neighbour instance embeddings). Classify by cosine similarity. Return 'unknown' when the best score is below a per-class threshold learned leave-one-out from stored exemplars, and prompt the user to label it. Then fit a logistic or cosine head on all stored exemplar embeddings (sklearn, under 1 s). RF evidence that prototypes work for modulation classes: MALWNN (arXiv 2503.18375) and FSOS-AMC (arXiv 2410.10265, few-shot open-set with meta-prototypes and an open-set classifier; AUROC gains claimed, numbers not on the abstract page).
    - **Versions and platform:** numpy, scikit-learn 1.9.1 and faiss-cpu 1.15.1 (only needed above about 10^5 vectors) on aarch64. Embedder as a QAIRT 2.42 context binary plus an ONNX FP32 copy.
    - **Limits and risks:** INT8 embeddings can collapse on this exact board. A Radxa user saw CLIP cosine similarity above 0.99 for everything and ArcFace at about 51% after INT8. Gate on INT8-vs-FP32 cosine parity, run the final FC and normalisation on the CPU, and try A16W8 or QAT, or run the embedder on the CPU (estimated 1-3 ms per crop). The 5/20/200 shot counts are rules of thumb, not measured.
    - **Sources:**
      - https://arxiv.org/abs/1712.07136
      - https://arxiv.org/abs/2503.18375
      - https://arxiv.org/abs/2410.10265
      - https://forum.radxa.com/t/dragon-q6a-qnn-htp-pipeline-working-but-int8-only-firmware-blocks-real-ml-workloads/31217
  7.
    - **Name:** Incremental detector: class-agnostic objectness on the NPU, last-layer class head on the CPU
    - **Role:** Adds classes to the detector without full retraining.
    - **Details:** Train the NPU detector at base for 'signal' objectness, box regression and about 8-10 generic families: analog FM/AM, FSK/GMSK/AFSK, PSK single-carrier, OFDM, bursty/pulsed, CW/tone, chirp, noise-like/spread, and spurs/RFI. Fine labels (Meteor LRPT, HRPT, APRS, CubeSat GMSK, RS41, ADS-B, AIS, SSTV, DVB-S2, GSM/LTE/Wi-Fi/BT interference, broadcast FM) live in the CPU stage-2 head. This mirrors WBSig53, which separates detection (presence, time, frequency) from recognition (adding the modulation family). TFA (arXiv 2003.06957) shows that fine-tuning only the last layer of a detector is the key to few-shot detection, beating meta-learning by about 2-20 points. Option: have the NPU emit per-location feature maps (e.g. 32x32x64 + 16x16x128 + 8x8x256 for a 256 px tile, about 112 KB INT8) and run a 1x1 class conv on the CPU (about 2.3 MMAC for 20 classes). That conv can be retrained or imprinted in seconds. Continual learning: keep an exemplar bank (embeddings plus SigMF references) and replay it whenever the head is refit (iCaRL, arXiv 1611.07725). Owfi et al. (arXiv 2312.04718) report that incremental-learning frameworks prevent catastrophic forgetting in modulation recognition. A signal the class-agnostic detector misses (low recall) cannot be fixed in the field and must be queued for a base retrain.
    - **Versions and platform:** Detector and head both exported from PyTorch. The head runs on onnxruntime 1.31 CPU or numpy.
    - **Limits and risks:** Objectness generalisation to unseen shapes (very wide OFDM, sub-bin CW) is unverified. Per-location INT8 features face the same quantisation-fidelity risk as the embeddings.
    - **Sources:**
      - https://arxiv.org/abs/2003.06957
      - https://arxiv.org/abs/2211.10335
      - https://arxiv.org/abs/1611.07725
      - https://arxiv.org/abs/2312.04718
  8.
    - **Name:** ONNX -> QAIRT 2.42 export, calibration and deployment path (exact commands)
    - **Role:** Turns any trained detector or embedder into an HTP context binary that matches the device runtime.
    - **Details:** Step 1, export: build static NCHW models (detector [1,1,256,256], embedder [1,1,64,64]) with Conv-BN-ReLU/ReLU6, nearest Resize and Concat. Give objectness, box and class logits separate outputs, and run decode/NMS on the CPU. Radxa users got all-zero YOLO outputs from a quantised concatenated head and fixed it by splitting outputs and dequantising each with its own scale. In PyTorch 2.14, torch.onnx.export defaults to dynamo=True (since 2.9) and external_data=True. Pin opset to the converter's range (the audit used 17), set external_data=False, and run onnx.checker plus an ORT parity check. Step 2, convert: 'qairt-converter --input_network m.onnx --output_path m.dlc'. With AIMET QAT, add '--quantization_overrides m.encodings'. Step 3, quantise: 'qairt-quantizer --input_dlc m.dlc --input_list calib.txt --output_dlc m_q.dlc --use_per_channel_quantization'. If accuracy drops, add --act_bitwidth 16 (A16W8, unverified on v68) and try --apply_algorithms cle. calib.txt lists 500-1000 raw float32 tiles (AI Hub recommendation; the audit used 300-500). Preprocessing must be identical (dB, noise-floor subtraction, clip, 0-1 scaling). Stratify the set across SDR, sample rate, gain, noise-only, strong-signal and every class. Step 4, context binary: 'qnn-context-binary-generator --model libQnnModelDlc.so --backend libQnnHtp.so --dlc_path m_q.dlc --output_dir out --binary_file m --config_file config_file.json'. config_backend.json uses dsp_arch v68, soc_id 35 and vtcm_mb 2; Radxa's example uses 0 (= max), but only about 2 MB is usable. Step 5, verify on the device: 'qnn-net-run --backend libQnnHtp.so --retrieve_context m.bin --input_list test.txt' and compare with ORT FP32. Step 6, ship a versioned bundle: context binary, FP32 ONNX, labels, prototypes, preprocessing parameters, calibration hash and QAIRT version string. Switch atomically and keep a rollback copy.
    - **Versions and platform:** QAIRT 2.42.0.251225 on an x86-64 Ubuntu 22.04 host. The current (2.5x) docs list arm-Linux Ubuntu 24.04 / Python 3.12 as a host with ONNX-only conversion, and Radxa publishes an ARM64 Docker image (radxazifeng278/qairt-npu-v68:v1.2, Ubuntu 24.04 base, 3.93 GB, contents undocumented). Whether on-device conversion works with 2.42 is unverified. Flags were checked against the Sep 2026 docs; confirm them with --help in 2.42.
    - **Limits and risks:** Acceptance gates (heuristics): detector mAP@0.5 within 2 points of FP32, per-class recall with no collapse, mean INT8/FP32 embedding cosine of at least 0.98, and few-shot accuracy within 2 points. If a model fails, use A16W8, then QAT, then CPU fallback. AIMET encodings vs 2.42 converter compatibility is untested.
    - **Sources:**
      - https://docs.radxa.com/en/dragon/q6a/app-dev/npu-dev/qairt-usage
      - https://docs.qualcomm.com/bundle/publicresource/80-63442-10/topics/SNPE_general_tools.md
      - https://docs.qualcomm.com/bundle/publicresource/80-63442-10/topics/qairt_quantizer.md
      - https://docs.qualcomm.com/bundle/publicresource/80-63442-10/topics/linux_setup.md
      - https://docs.pytorch.org/docs/2.14/onnx_export.html
      - https://forum.radxa.com/t/yolov8n-context-binary-generation-for-q6a/30899
      - https://forum.radxa.com/t/issues-running-yolov8n-with-qairt-sdk-2-49-on-radxa-dragon-q6a-qcs6490/31462
      - https://hub.docker.com/r/radxazifeng278/qairt-npu-v68

    - **Name:** Op support and measured QCS6490 detector latencies (for sizing what you train)
    - **Role:** Constrains the architecture so it quantises and runs on the HTP, and sets frames-per-second expectations.
    - **Details:** The QNN SupportedOps table marks HTP INT8 and INT16 'YES' for Conv2d, DepthWiseConv2d, Batchnorm, Relu, ReluMinMax (Clip), Sigmoid, HardSwish, Resize/ResizeNearestNeighbor, Concat, Split, StridedSlice, PoolMax2d/PoolAvg2d, FullyConnected, MatMul, L2Norm, LayerNorm, Softmax, Transpose and TransposeConv2d. This is the generic table; FP16 does not apply to v68. Qualcomm AI Hub model cards, measured on QCS6490 (Proxy) at 640x640: YOLOv8n-det w8a8 QNN_DLC 4.0 ms and w8a16 10.5 ms (A16 costs about 2.6x); Yolo-X (Apache-2.0, 8.98 M parameters) w8a8 7.1 ms; MobileNet-v2 224 w8a8 1.3 ms. On real Q6A boards with 2.42, Radxa users measured 10-12 ms for the official YOLOv8n binary and about 20 ms for a custom one. A 256x256 single-channel tile detector (about 0.4-0.7 GMAC) should therefore take a few ms on the HTP (extrapolated, not measured).
    - **Versions and platform:** Model cards are from qai-hub-models v0.64.0 (AI Hub default QAIRT, not 2.42).
    - **Limits and risks:** Proxy and newer-SDK numbers are optimistic for 2.42 firmware. Long-run HTP hangs (about 1 h) and the 0x80000600 FastRPC failures need the watchdog and CPU fallback from the audit.
    - **Sources:**
      - https://docs.qualcomm.com/bundle/publicresource/80-63442-10/topics/SupportedOps.md
      - https://huggingface.co/qualcomm/YOLOv8-Detection
